newsitem.title: USA: GM to let Schott sell auto dealership.
newsitem.headline: GM to let Schott sell auto dealership.

text.p: Cincinnati Reds owner Marge Schott, under fire from General Motors for allegedly falsifying auto sales records, will be able to complete the sale of a Chevrolet dealership rather than be stripped of the business, the company said Monday.
In a meeting with a hearing officer for the state board that licenses auto dealers, GM said if it approves the terms of the sale, its dispute with Schott will be settled.
GM last month accused her of falsifying 1995 car sales records to meet sales goals.
The normally outspoken Schott, 68, did not attend the public meeting. Her lawyer declined to talk with reporters.
In a statement last week, Schott said she has a deal in the works to sell the suburban Cincinnati Chevrolet-Geo dealership to another auto dealer in the area.

Already banned by Major League Baseball from day-to-day operations of the Reds, she was accused by GM of using names of friends and employees as fictitious car buyers in 57 sales, then hiding cars on her estate.
Schott has not responded to the allegations. The National League has said it will see if league action is warranted.

Baseball banned the chain-smoking Schott, its only female team owner, from running her ballclub through 1998 after remarks she made about Adolf Hitler, African-Americans, working women and Jews. She had also been suspended in 1993.
Schott has until Feb. 20 to sell the dealership although she could request an extension, the hearing officer for the Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles Dealers Board said.
Schott will keep a separate Buick dealership which GM said is not involved in the controversy.
